label: MiG-29A Fulcrum (DCS DTC)
pathSyntax: Dot-separated keys of the .dtc "data" object. "[]" = any array index, "{}" = any object key, each as its own segment (e.g. NAV.[].waypoints.[].lat, CMDS.CMDSProgramSettings.{}.Priority). An array/object is user-extensible only when its section has a "template"; "maxItems"/"fixedLength" bound it ("fixedLength" on an object = number of keys, all required). "{index}" in itemLabel is 1-based. "itemLabels" (array) names fixed array slots in order; "keyLabels" names object keys. A field with "optional": true is absent from a fresh cartridge (Lua nil) and may stay absent. Sections marked hidden cover a whole derived/internal subtree. "display" = {unit, factor, decimals}: shown value = stored value * factor. For kind string, "maxLength"/"pattern" constrain the text.
source: DCS 2.9.30.28738 CoreMods/aircraft/MiG-29-Fulcrum/DTC (MiG-29 Fulcrum_DTC.lua, NAV/*.lua, Weapon/*.lua, Radio/*.lua, ADF/*.lua) + DCS MiG-29A Flight Manual; see native-MiG-29 Fulcrum.md and EXPORT-NOTES.md

sections.label: MiG-29A Fulcrum cartridge
sections.help: Root of data. Three independent programs (Program_1..3) each hold the SN-29 navigation data (points, steer points, airfields, RSBN beacons, route), weapon settings, CMDS/SPO-15, R-862 radio and ARK-19 ADF presets. SelectedProgram picks the one that is loaded. All NAV lists are terrain-locked.

sections.label: Program 1
sections.help: Program 1: complete set of SN-29 navigation, weapon, CMDS/SPO-15, R-862 and ARK-19 data. NAV lists are terrain-gated and must be JSON arrays (an object with "1","2" keys crashes setData). The exporter writes the planned route here.

sections.label: Pre-planned point database (PNT)
sections.help: Point database the other NAV lists copy from (in the ME every steer point, airfield-from-point, RSBN-from-point and route entry is picked from here). Generated by the exporter from the planned route. No count limit. Numbering is positional: num = name = "PNT"+index; id is a stable unique map id.

sections.label: Steer points (WPT 1-3)
sections.help: The three steer points the SN-29 uses for point-to-point navigation (WP/A-D buttons 1-3). Max 3 (the ME refuses a 4th). Each is a copy of a Points entry. The exporter uses the first three en-route points of the plan (not the take-off/landing airfields) unless the user picks others.

sections.label: Airfields (ARD 1-3)
sections.help: The three airfields for RETURN / landing approach (A/D buttons). Max 3. type "Airdrome" = a theatre airfield (name must equal the terrain airdrome display name; its runways/PRMG channels drive the approach); type "Point" = a copy of a Points entry. The exporter writes the departure, destination and alternate airfields of the plan when the planner knows the airfield and its runways; otherwise it leaves this [] for the pilot to fill in the ME.

sections.label: Runways
sections.help: Runway ends of a theatre airfield, sorted alphanumerically, id = 1-based position. [] for type Point. The ME refreshes channel from the theatre ILS/PRMG beacons on load.

sections.label: RSBN beacons (1-3)
sections.help: Three RSBN short-range nav beacons used for position correction and RETURN. type "RSBN" entries must reference an rsbn_beacon unit of the SAME mission (unitId and name = "<unit name>_P<route point index>", channel from its ActivateRSBN action): the ME DELETES any entry with unitId != 0 that does not match a beacon of the mission, together with route entries pointing at it. Not generated by the exporter (the planner cannot know the mission beacons). type "Point" with unitId 0 survives but carries no channel.

sections.label: Route planning
sections.help: Ordered route built from rows of the four lists above (each entry references a PNT/WPT/ARD/RSBN row by num). The ME uses it for the route line, ETAs, route length and average speed; whether the aircraft loads it beyond the 3 steer points is not documented. No count limit. The exporter writes one entry per planned waypoint.

sections.label: Target point
sections.help: Weapon target point (Weapon tab "Target Point" / "Target Elevation"), picked from Points. Empty = [] in a fresh cartridge; when it has no name and Points is non-empty, the ME sets it to Points[1] the next time the page is filled. Terrain-gated, copied verbatim on import. The exporter sets it to the plan's target point, else the first point.

sections.label: Weapon settings
sections.help: Weapon tab settings. A fresh cartridge has [] (empty table); write {"trainingMode": false} or true.

sections.label: CMDS (flares) and SPO-15 launch warnings
sections.help: Flare dispensing programs and forced SPO-15LM launch warnings. All values are 1-based INDEXES into fixed lists (option labels give the real value). Not terrain-gated; merged field by field on import.

sections.label: SPO-15LM additional launch warnings
sections.help: Array of exactly 6, one per SPO-15 threat type in this order: 1 = П (P): LPRF fire-control radar with CW illuminator in SA guidance mode (F-4, Aegis ships); usually a launch; 2 = З (Z): AAA / short and medium range SAM fire-control radar (Vulcan); 3 = Х (H): CW radar, HPRF radars at low power (Hawk CWAR/HIPIR); 4 = Н (N): Strategic SAM search and fire-control radar (Nike-Hercules); 5 = F (Ф): 4th-generation HPRF fighter radar (F-14, F-15, F-16); 6 = С (S): LPRF fire-control radar with the CW channel off, LPRF fighter FCR, surveillance and other radars (F-4, F-5, Mirage F1, naval). Forces a launch warning for that type on detection (On) or on lock (Lock).

sections.label: VHF/UHF radio R-862 presets
sections.help: Channel_0..Channel_19. Replaced WHOLESALE on import: all 20 keys must be present, each with freq and modulation, or setData crashes (Radio.lua:81). Loaded only when mirror_Radio is false.

sections.label: ARK-19 ADF presets
sections.help: Four channels, each an outer (far) and inner (near) NDB. Replaced WHOLESALE on import: all 8 keys with freq and modulation must be present or setData crashes. Loaded only when mirror_ADF is false. Defaults: 1 = 625/303, 2 = 525/1065, 3 = 489/995, 4 = 870/490 kHz (outer/inner).

fields.label: Aircraft type
fields.help: Must be exactly "MiG-29 Fulcrum" (space, no A; display name "MiG-29A Fulcrum"). Anything else imports nothing.

fields.label: Internal cartridge name
fields.help: Cosmetic. ED files have "". DCS indexes cartridges by the outer .dtc "name"; the exporter may write the same string here.

fields.label: Theatre
fields.help: Theatre id of the mission (miz "theatre", e.g. Caucasus, Nevada, PersianGulf, Syria, MarianaIslands, Kola, Afghanistan, GermanyCW). NAV data (Points, Waypoints, Airdromes, RSBN, Route, TargetPoint) of every program is imported ONLY when this equals the current map; otherwise the ME warns and drops it. "" in a fresh cartridge; the ME rewrites it on save.

fields.label: Program to load
fields.help: Which of the three programs the aircraft loads ("Load Prgm N" radio button). Default Program_1, which is the one the exporter fills from the route.

fields.label: Do not upload NAV (SN-29) data
fields.help: INVERTED flag (dlg label "Do not upload tab data"): true = the navigation tab is NOT uploaded to the aircraft and its panels are greyed out in the ME. A fresh ME cartridge has true. The exporter sets false whenever it writes route data.

fields.label: Do not upload R-862 presets
fields.help: INVERTED: true = the radio presets in the cartridge are NOT loaded (the aircraft keeps the mission presets). Fresh cartridge: true. Set false only when the user edited the presets.

fields.label: Do not upload ARK-19 presets
fields.help: INVERTED: true = the ADF presets are NOT loaded. Fresh cartridge: true. Set false only when the user edited them.

fields.label: Map id
fields.help: Stable unique id "PNT<k>"; the ME takes 1 + the digits of the previous last id, so ids can skip. Waypoints/Route/TargetPoint copy it. Exporter: "PNT"+index.

fields.label: Number
fields.help: "PNT"+index (1-based). setData recomputes it from the position.

fields.label: Name
fields.help: "PNT"+index. Waypoints[].name, Route[].name and TargetPoint.name reference points by this string. Not defaulted by setData: always write it.

fields.label: Note
fields.help: Free label up to 7 characters (ED uses e.g. BULLS, STRYK, FYTTR). Exporter default: the planner waypoint name, upper-case ASCII, cut to 7.

fields.label: Map X (north)
fields.help: DCS map metres, x = north. MUST be a number (the ME does arithmetic on it, e.g. math.floor(x + 0.5); nil or non-numeric throws). No lat/lon is stored anywhere in this cartridge.

fields.label: Map Y (east)
fields.help: DCS map metres, y = east. Must be a number.

fields.label: Altitude
fields.help: Planned altitude, metres MSL (default 2000). Copied into steer points and route entries. The ME ft toggle is display only.

fields.label: Speed
fields.help: Planned speed, km/h (default 790). Copied into steer points and route entries.

fields.label: Ground elevation
fields.help: Terrain height at x/y in metres (the ME stores getAltitude(x, y) when the point is placed). Becomes TargetPoint.altitude when the point is the target.

fields.label: Number
fields.help: "WPT"+index; recomputed by setData. Route entries reference the steer point by this num.

fields.label: Source point id
fields.help: Map id of the copied Points entry ("PNT<k>"). ED files sometimes omit it; write it.

fields.label: From point
fields.help: Always true (copied from a point; the ME then does not draw it separately).

fields.label: Source point
fields.help: Name of the copied point ("PNT<i>").

fields.label: Note
fields.help: Free label up to 7 characters.

fields.label: Map X (north)
fields.help: Copied from the point, DCS map metres.

fields.label: Map Y (east)
fields.help: Copied from the point, DCS map metres.

fields.label: Altitude
fields.help: Metres MSL, copied from the point.

fields.label: Speed
fields.help: km/h, copied from the point.

fields.label: Number
fields.help: "ARD"+index; recomputed by setData.

fields.label: Map id
fields.help: Unique id "ARD<k>".

fields.label: Airfield
fields.help: type Airdrome: exact terrain airdrome display_name (e.g. "Sukhumi-Babushara", "Nellis", "Andersen AFB"); used to refresh PRMG channels and to find unit_name. type Point: the point name ("PNT<i>").

fields.label: Airfield unit name
fields.help: Terrain airdrome names.en (usually equal to name); "" for type Point. If absent setData looks it up from name. Used for the landing course.

fields.label: Note
fields.help: Free label up to 7 characters.

fields.label: Kind
fields.help: "Airdrome" (theatre airfield with runways) or "Point" (copied from Points, no runways). Missing = "Point".

fields.label: From point
fields.help: true on type Point entries only.

fields.label: Map X (north)
fields.help: Airfield reference point (or the point), DCS map metres.

fields.label: Map Y (east)
fields.help: DCS map metres.

fields.label: Altitude
fields.help: 0 for theatre airfields (ME default); the point altitude for type Point.

fields.label: Speed
fields.help: km/h, default 790 (copied into route entries).

fields.label: Landing runway
fields.help: Runway end used for the approach, equal to one runways[].text (e.g. "12", "21L", "06L"); "" for type Point.

fields.label: Index
fields.help: 1-based position in the sorted list.

fields.label: Runway end
fields.help: Runway side name, e.g. "12", "30", "06L".

fields.label: ILS course
fields.help: Course from the ILS beacon data; -361 = unknown (runways without ILS data).

fields.label: Airfield
fields.help: Airfield display name.

fields.label: PRMG channel
fields.help: PRMG/ILS channel number, -1 = none. After a manual edit in the ME it is stored as a 1-2 digit STRING with editableChannel true; write a number.

fields.label: Channel edited
fields.help: Set by the ME when the pilot typed a channel. Omit.

fields.label: Map id
fields.help: Unique id "RSBN<k>".

fields.label: Number
fields.help: "RSBN"+index; recomputed by setData.

fields.label: Beacon unit id
fields.help: Mission unitId of the rsbn_beacon unit (type RSBN) or 0 (type Point). A non-zero id that does not exist in the mission makes the ME delete the entry.

fields.label: Beacon
fields.help: Beacon display name exactly as the ME lists it ("<unit name>_P<n>", e.g. "Sukhumi-Babushara_P1"), or the point name for type Point.

fields.label: Note
fields.help: Free label up to 7 characters.

fields.label: RSBN channel
fields.help: Beacon channel (from the beacon; the ME refreshes it on load). Absent for type Point.

fields.label: Kind
fields.help: "RSBN" or "Point". Missing = "Point".

fields.label: From point
fields.help: true on type Point entries only.

fields.help: Beacon position, DCS map metres (refreshed from the beacon on load).

fields.label: Map Y (east)
fields.help: DCS map metres.

fields.help: Default 0.

fields.label: Speed
fields.help: km/h, default 790.

fields.label: Source row
fields.help: num of the referenced row: "PNT<i>", "WPT<i>", "ARD<i>" or "RSBN<i>". Deleting/renumbering a row in the ME updates or removes matching route entries.

fields.label: Source id
fields.help: id of the referenced row (map highlight).

fields.label: Source name
fields.help: name of the referenced row (e.g. "PNT3", "Sukhumi-Babushara").

fields.label: Note
fields.help: Free label up to 7 characters.

fields.label: Map X (north)
fields.help: Copied from the referenced row, DCS map metres.

fields.label: Map Y (east)
fields.help: Copied from the referenced row, DCS map metres.

fields.label: Altitude
fields.help: Planned altitude in metres (UI max 5 digits). Interpreted per alt_type.

fields.label: Altitude reference
fields.help: 1 MSL (default), 2 AGL.

fields.label: Speed
fields.help: Planned speed in km/h (UI max 4 digits); 0 makes the ME ETA computation return -1.

fields.label: Speed type
fields.help: 1 IAS (default), 2 GS, 3 TAS. The ME combo has no handler: the value is stored but not used by the ME.

fields.label: ETA
fields.help: Absolute time of day in seconds (d*86400 + h*3600 + m*60 + s, same base as the mission start time). Kept as written only when FIX_Time is true; otherwise the ME recomputes it whenever the DTC page is open.

fields.label: Fix time
fields.help: Lock this ETA (a planned time over / time on target).

fields.label: Point id
fields.help: id of the chosen Points entry. Optional.

fields.label: Target
fields.help: name of the chosen Points entry ("PNT<i>").

fields.label: Map X (north)
fields.help: Copied from the point.

fields.label: Map Y (east)
fields.help: Copied from the point.

fields.label: Target elevation
fields.help: Ground elevation at the target in metres (the ME uses getAltitude(x, y)).

fields.label: Training mode
fields.help: Weapons training mode. Must be set before take-off (manual).

fields.label: Burst count I
fields.help: Flares per burst, setting I. Stored as the 1-based list index (default 1 = 1).

fields.label: Burst count II
fields.help: Flares per burst, setting II. Stored as the 1-based list index (default 1 = 1).

fields.label: Burst interval
fields.help: Seconds between bursts. Stored as the 1-based list index (default 1 = 0.5 s).

fields.label: Salvo interval
fields.help: Seconds between salvos. Stored as the 1-based list index (default 1 = 5 s).

fields.label: Salvo count - AIR
fields.help: Number of salvos in the AIR (air threat) program. Stored as the 1-based list index (default 1 = 1).

fields.label: Salvo count - GROUND
fields.help: Number of salvos in the GROUND (ZRK, SAM) program. Stored as the 1-based list index (default 1 = 6).

fields.label: Launch warning
fields.help: 1 Off (default), 2 On (warn on detection), 3 Lock (warn on lock).

fields.label: Modulation
fields.help: 1 AM (default), 2 FM.

fields.label: Frequency
fields.help: NDB frequency in kHz, 150.000-1299.500.

derived.formula: data.terrain = mission theatre id (miz "theatre"); exactly the string DCS uses (case-sensitive)

pts = route.points (all planned waypoints, in order; take-off/landing airfields may be included as points too).
Points = pts.map((p, i) => ({ id: "PNT" + (i + 1), num: "PNT" + (i + 1), name: "PNT" + (i + 1),
  note: ascii(p.name).toUpperCase().slice(0, 7), x: p.x, y: p.y,
  alt: Math.round(p.alt_m ?? 2000), speed: Math.round(p.speed_kmh ?? 790), terrainAltitude: Math.round(groundElevation_m(p.x, p.y)) }))
x, y = theatreProjection(lat, lon) (DCS map metres, x north, y east). Numbers only.

steer = user choice, else the first 3 points that are not the departure/arrival airfield.
Waypoints = steer.slice(0, 3).map((pt, k) => ({ num: "WPT" + (k + 1), id: pt.id, geo: true, name: pt.name, note: "", x: pt.x, y: pt.y, alt: pt.alt, speed: pt.speed }))

For departure, destination, alternate (max 3, skip unknown/duplicates) with terrain airdrome data ad:
{ num: "ARD" + k, id: "ARD" + k, name: ad.display_name, unit_name: ad.names_en ?? ad.display_name, note: "", type: "Airdrome",
  x: ad.reference_point.x, y: ad.reference_point.y, alt: 0, speed: 790, selectedRunwaySide: landingRunwayEnd,
  runways: sortAlnum(ad.runwayEnds).map((r, j) => ({ id: j + 1, text: r.name, direction: r.ilsCourse ?? -361, display_name: ad.display_name, channel: r.prmgChannel ?? -1 })) }
An airfield without runway data cannot be added in the ME either: leave it out. Without terrain data write [].

Route = pts.map((p, i) => { const ref = steerOf(p) ?? airdromeOf(p) ?? Points[i];  // prefer WPT/ARD row when p is one
  return { num: ref.num, id: ref.id, name: ref.name, note: "", x: ref.x, y: ref.y, alt: Points[i].alt, alt_type: p.agl ? 2 : 1,
    speed: Points[i].speed, speed_type: 1, ETA: eta(i), FIX_Time: !!p.fixedTime }; })
eta(i) = mission start seconds-of-day + planned elapsed seconds to p (ED style: first point = start time). Only FIX_Time entries survive the ME recomputation.
ETA = startTimeOfDay_s + elapsed_s(i). The ME recomputes non-fixed ETAs as prev.ETA + dist_m / speed_kmh (unit-mixed, ignore it). Seconds since 00:00 of the mission day; add 86400 per day.
tp = plan target point ?? Points[0]; TargetPoint = { id: tp.id, name: tp.name, x: tp.x, y: tp.y, altitude: tp.terrainAltitude }; with no points write [] (empty).
mirror_NAV = !(Program_1 has Points)  // false = upload. mirror_Radio / mirror_ADF = false only when the user edited that tab.

num = name = "PNT" + (index + 1); Waypoints num "WPT" + (index + 1); Airdromes "ARD" + ...; RSBN "RSBN" + ... (setData recomputes num from position; cross-references use num/name, so keep them positional)
